Pick out the candidates that are anagrams of a word, ignoring case, where a word is not an anagram of itself.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/anagram) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: anagram.nomi
/// The candidates that are anagrams of `subject`, in their original order.
/// Letter case does not matter, and a word is not an anagram of itself.
pub fn find(subject: String, candidates: List<String>) -> List<String> {
    subject = String.fold_case(subject)
    letters = Iter.sort(subject)

    candidates
    |> Iter.filter(fn candidate -> {
        candidate = String.fold_case(candidate)
        candidate != subject and Iter.sort(candidate) == letters
    })
    |> Iter.to_list()
}

// FILE: anagram_test.nomi
import anagram

test "finds anagrams" {
    cases = [
        #("no matches", "diaper", ["hello", "world", "zombies", "pants"], []),
        #("detects two anagrams", "solemn", ["lemons", "cherry", "melons"], ["lemons", "melons"]),
        #("does not detect anagram subsets", "good", ["dog", "goody"], []),
        #("detects anagram", "listen", ["enlists", "google", "inlets", "banana"], ["inlets"]),
        #(
            "detects three anagrams",
            "allergy",
            ["gallery", "ballerina", "regally", "clergy", "largely", "leading"],
            ["gallery", "regally", "largely"],
        ),
        #(
            "detects multiple anagrams with different case",
            "nose",
            ["Eons", "ONES"],
            ["Eons", "ONES"],
        ),
        #("does not detect non-anagrams with identical checksum", "mass", ["last"], []),
        #(
            "detects anagrams case-insensitively",
            "Orchestra",
            ["cashregister", "Carthorse", "radishes"],
            ["Carthorse"],
        ),
        #(
            "detects anagrams using case-insensitive subject",
            "Orchestra",
            ["cashregister", "carthorse", "radishes"],
            ["carthorse"],
        ),
        #(
            "detects anagrams using case-insensitive possible matches",
            "orchestra",
            ["cashregister", "Carthorse", "radishes"],
            ["Carthorse"],
        ),
        #("does not detect an anagram if the original word is repeated", "go", ["goGoGO"], []),
        #("anagrams must use all letters exactly once", "tapper", ["patter"], []),
        #("words are not anagrams of themselves", "BANANA", ["BANANA"], []),
        #(
            "words are not anagrams of themselves even if letter case is partially different",
            "BANANA",
            ["Banana"],
            [],
        ),
        #(
            "words are not anagrams of themselves even if letter case is completely different",
            "BANANA",
            ["banana"],
            [],
        ),
        #(
            "words other than themselves can be anagrams",
            "LISTEN",
            ["LISTEN", "Silent"],
            ["Silent"],
        ),
        #("handles case of greek letters", "ΑΒΓ", ["ΒΓΑ", "ΒΓΔ", "γβα", "αβγ"], ["ΒΓΑ", "γβα"]),
        #("different characters may have the same bytes", "a⬂", ["€a"], []),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, subject, candidates, expected), description {
        assert anagram.find(subject, candidates) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The anagram key is `Iter.sort(word)`: a `String` iterates by grapheme, so sorting it gives a `List<String>` to compare, with no codepoint conversion.
- Case is ignored with `String.fold_case` on both sides, once for the subject and once per candidate. Folding is Unicode's caseless matching, which `String.to_lower` only approximates: the two Greek sigmas `ς` and `σ` fold to one letter and lower-case to two.
- All 18 current cases are one `subtests` table, since every row is the same call and comparison. The four cases that newer ones reimplement are left out.
- Each row carries its canonical description as its first column and is named by it (`subtests cases, #(description, subject, candidates, expected), description`), so a failing row reports under its description.
